title: Adaptive tier failover with region-aware grace periods and variant downgrade
creator: Marco Chen
description: Problem: customers running on Dedicated capacity experience temporary capacity holes (maintenance, noisy neighbors, preemption) which currently cause either immediate spillover to Hosted (higher cost and sometimes higher latency) or blunt throttling. Both outcomes create either cost spikes or poor latency/availability. Goal: implement an adaptive failover policy that introduces region-aware grace periods, tenant-priority decay, and controlled model-variant downgrades to smooth transitions between Dedicated and Hosted while minimizing cost and avoiding oscillation. This ticket focusses on the routing/orchestrator side: scoring capacity, enforcing time-bounded grace windows, and applying progressive downgrade steps (quantized weight -> smaller model -> hosted) instead of single-step cutovers.
acceptance_criteria: Grace-period mechanism that postpones mandatory spillover for configurable windows per-region and per-tenant (defaults: 30s per-hosted-region, 10s for intra-region failures)
Capacity scoring produced by orchestrator that combines available GPU slots, recent error spikes, and queue depth into a single capacity_score [0-100] used by policy decisions

Tiered downgrade sequence implemented: (1) reduce max-concurrency and enable prefix/KV cache fast-paths; (2) route to quantized model variant; (3) downgrade to smaller model variant; (4) spill to Hosted — each step has configurable thresholds and cooldowns
No oscillation observed in synthetic load tests: repeated failing Dedicated nodes do not cause repeated oscillation within a 5-minute test window
Failures and decisions are logged to per-tenant tracing with reason codes for postmortem (capacity_shortfall | variant_quality | latency_sla_breach | config_override)
Forward/rollback hooks for canary: feature flag to enable adaptive failover per-customer and ability to quickly disable globally with single runtime flag
engineering_notes: We will implement a capacity_score API on the capacity-proxy that returns a small JSON blob (score, reason_tags, freshness_ms). Orchestrator will consume and cache this score for 5s.

Grace-window semantics: per-request route decision consults last N scores (N configurable, default 3) and only triggers downgrade if all N scores fall below threshold or if an explicit failure (node error) occurs and grace_window expired.

Variant downgrade weights: use exponential backoff style weighting (full -> q8_ggml -> q4_ggml -> small-model) so we can route percentage of requests to cheaper variants to measure quality impact before full cutover.
Introduce tenant_priority_decay to lower spillover precedence for low-priority tenants over time if they repeatedly trigger expensive hosted spillovers; decays back after quiet period.
Add metrics: routing.decision_count, routing.downgrade_steps, routing.oscillation_events, routing.spillover_cost_delta, plus existing latency/p95 and error-rate metrics tagged by tenant and region.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (short-term, 1 sprint): capacity_score endpoint (capacity-proxy) + orchestrator support for grace_window and basic downgrade sequence flags
Phase 2 (2 sprints): progressive variant rollout with percentages, tenant_priority_decay, and logging enrichments (reason codes). Instrument dashboards and alerts.
Phase 3 (1 sprint): integrate with rollout system for canary enablement, add automated rollback and safety circuit-breaker based on cost and quality signals
PRs: backend service changes (capacity-proxy), orchestrator policy delta, runtime feature-flag plumbing, metrics dashboard updates
Config knobs: grace_window_ms, min_score_threshold, downgrade_order, downgrade_percentage_step, cooldown_ms, tenant_decay_halflife
progress_updates: 2026-02-22: Kickoff sync with infra, runtime, and product. Agreed on capacity_score contract and default thresholds.
2026-02-28: capacity-proxy prototype implemented returning synthetic score. Basic orchestrator branch created to read score and apply 30s grace_window.
2026-03-05: Spike completed for percentage-based variant routing. Found timing edge where oscillation occurred when grace_window < 10s under bursty traffic.
2026-03-09: Adjusted default grace_window to 30s for cross-region and 10s for intra-region after perf experiments. Started integration tests for synthetic oscillation scenario.
2026-03-10: Demo to PM & SRE. PM requested addition of tenant_priority_decay and a cost-safety circuit. SRE requested explicit reason codes in traces (done).
review_feedback: PM (Elena Ortiz): prefer smaller default windows but allow per-customer override; requested explicit per-customer billing alert if hosted spillover cost > 15% of baseline
SRE (Owen Park): add circuit-breaker that triggers if hosted_latency_p95 > SLA for 3 consecutive minutes — fallback should be to throttling rather than further spillover
Design (Nina Alvarez): want UX hooks surfaced in Console for per-tenant grace window and downgrade aggressiveness and a timeline view of recent routing decisions
risks: Quality regressions: routing to quantized or smaller variants may degrade customer-perceived quality — must be monitored and have immediate rollback.
Cost complexity: percentage-based routing to Hosted for measurement increases cost during experiments; need budget guardrails per-tenant.
Oscillation: incorrect cooldown/grace settings could cause repeated failover loops; tests must include bursty start/stop patterns.
Operational complexity: many new knobs per-tenant can increase support burden; default safe presets required.
test_plan: Unit tests for capacity_score consumer and grace_window logic
Integration test: simulate Dedicated node drop and assert that downgrade sequence respects configured timings and that no oscillation occurs within 5 minutes
Load test: mixed tenant load with low/high priority tenants to validate tenant_priority_decay and cost-safety triggers
Canary run: enable feature for 5 internal customers and monitor metrics and customer reported quality for 72 hours
Chaos test: randomly kill Dedicated pool members and validate decision logs, reason codes, and that automated rollback triggers on quality/cost signals
notes: If we see unacceptable quality delta on quantized variants, we will add an experiment to send a small sampled subset of requests to Hosted for direct quality comparison before a full spillover.
Coordinate with pricing team to add an alert when estimated monthly spillover cost > 20% of committed Dedicated spend for a tenant.
